translation.english_title: The trouble of having no work

english_lines: The trouble of having no work,
Has gone away like morning dew...
A good life I had never imagined,
Came and joined me of its own accord,
This is a fine day of joy,
This is a golden day of wealth...
Those I had never known before came as kin, just as my heart wished,
So that my sorrow may leave me,
They came today to bring me good,
Thinking me a seemaatti, they were deceived,
Ah, what a wonder this is...
notes: `வேலை யில்லாத` remains the explicit unemployment/no-work condition rather than being generalized to hardship.
`சீமாட்டி` is retained as `seemaatti` because the source's social-rank flavour is stronger than a neutral `lady`; the surrounding line makes the mistaken-status joke clear.
The joined source form `எனமனம்போலவே` is translated conservatively from context without altering the Tamil witness.

translator_notes: The song moves quickly from unemployment to unexpected prosperity and mistaken social status; that sudden reversal is retained without smoothing it into a general happiness lyric.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
